title: SLO economics - heatfunnel scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
Quick experimental sketch to explore a small 'heat-funnel' view: show how p50/p95/p99 shift as we trade latency SLOs for unit-cost (per-1k tokens) by changing batching, cache hit, and quant profiles. Aim is a one-pager that product/console folks can iterate into a chart for the Console's SLO-cost tooltip.

High-level takeaways (working):
- SmallBatch (BS=1) gives lowest p50 but cost is ~3x of opportunistic batching at steady state.
- Aggressive quant (8-bit dynamic) reduces cost ~25% but increases p99 by 10–15ms for tails under microbursts.
- KV cache hit > 60% moves the entire heat-funnel left (better latency) and compresses cost significantly.

Experimental setup:
- models: redwood-micro-7B, redwood-core-13B-q8, llama2-13b-8bit (reference)
- hardware: n1-standard + A100 equivalent; sessions multiplexed across 8 vcores (mini pool)
- traffic: realistic sessionized mix: 70% short-turn (<=50 tokens), 30% long-turn (200–400 tokens), poisson bursts (lambda spikes at +4x for 30s every 10m)
- knobs: batching window (0ms/5ms/20ms), batch size cap (1/8/32), quant profile (fp16/q8_dynamic), kv cache ON/OFF
- cost calc: amortized GPU cost + infra overhead -> reported as $/1k tokens (approx, internal rates)

Key table (excerpt):

Scenario | p50 ms | p95 ms | p99 ms | $/1k tok
-------- | ------:| ------:| ------:| ------:
BS=1, KV=OFF, fp16        | 48    | 290   | 520   | 3.22
BS=8, KV=OFF, fp16        | 62    | 330   | 680   | 1.45
BS=8, KV=ON(65%), fp16    | 44    | 220   | 410   | 1.03
BS=8, KV=ON(65%), q8     | 50    | 260   | 470   | 0.78
BS=32, KV=ON(65%), q8    | 72    | 410   | 920   | 0.54

Observations:
- Moving from BS=1 to BS=8 reduced unit-cost by ~2.2x but increased p50 by ~15ms.
- Enabling KV cache with a 65% hit rate both improves latency and lowers cost (cache wins are multiplicative with batching).
- q8_dynamic yields biggest cost drop but exposes heavier tails under burst; p99 delta vs fp16 is material (approx +10–20%).

Simple ASCII heat-funnel (latency on X axis, cost depth):
(cost high) [|||||||||||||||] p99-heavy  -> BS=1, fp16
            [||||||||||   ] p95-mid      -> BS=8, fp16
(cost low)  [|||          ] p50-light    -> BS=32, q8 + KV

Microburst note (30s spikes):
- Under spike we saw p99 jump 2–3x for BS>=8 when prewarming disabled. Prewarm reduces spike p99 by ~35% but increases baseline cost by ~8%.

Questions / TODOs:
- Validate results on different hardware gen (V100 vs A100 vs H100) — tail behaviour likely hardware-sensitive.
- Re-run with client-side streaming (chunked response) to see tail smoothing effect.
- Produce a single-panel visualization: X=latency p95, Y=cost $/1k, bubble=size=burst-risk (p99/p95 ratio).
- Get product input: which SLO metric should we expose by default? p95 or p99? (ask @Sofia)
